title: Pagasa 19 mungbean (NSIC Mg 12): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Pagasa 19 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Pagasa 19 mungbean is a mungbean variety. 58 to 60 days to harvest, 1.2 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Pagasa 19 is a registered mungbean variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mg 12. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Mg 12. IPB UPLB CA, College, Laguna bred it. It takes 58 to 60 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 1.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.caption: Key facts of Pagasa 19
rows: Both the wet and the dry season

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Pagasa 19 mungbean takes 58 to 60 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.24 t/ha matches the average of its group, 1.25. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 58 to 60 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 5.5 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is glossy green. The seed holds 22.5 percent crude protein.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.27 t/ha dry season, 1.21 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** Glossy green seed, about 5 to 5.5 g per 100 seeds, crude protein about 22.5 percent.
Moderately resistant to Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a later Pag asa munggo with resistance to powdery mildew, recommended for both seasons. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Pagasa 19 mungbean

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: Is NSIC Mg 12 the same as Pagasa 19?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mg 12 is another name for Pagasa 19, registered as NSIC 2002 Mg 12. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 58 to 60 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pagasa 19?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
